desc:
Wix app development with the Wix CLI turns your idea into an installable app for Wix sites and stores. Ecom Swift LLC builds the dashboard page, the site widget and the backend, then hands you the code, a test site and a submission checklist.

## What is Wix app development?

Wix app development is the work of building software that site owners can install on their Wix sites. A typical app has three parts: a dashboard page where the owner manages settings, a site widget that appears on their live pages, and a backend that stores data and runs logic. The Wix CLI is the toolkit that scaffolds, runs and packages those parts so the app installs cleanly.

## Why build a Wix app instead of a one-off site feature

A custom feature on a single site helps one owner. An app packages the same idea so many owners can add it in a few clicks, each with their own settings and data. That is the difference between a service you deliver by hand and a product that scales across sites.

Wix also brings you a place to be found. Site owners already browse the App Market when they need a feature, so a well-made app can reach people who never heard of you. The catch is that site owners judge quickly. An app that installs badly, looks out of place or breaks in the editor is removed just as quickly.

## How build quality shapes your outcome

Your first users decide whether the app has a future. If the dashboard feels clumsy, they stop setting it up. If the widget slows the page or breaks on a phone, they uninstall it. If data is lost during an update, they tell others.

Building on current Wix tooling avoids many of these problems. Dashboard pages that use the Wix Design System look familiar to owners. Widgets built for the editor can be placed, styled and resized the way owners expect. Data stored in a proper collection survives updates. Whether Wix approves a listing, and how many owners install it, depends on factors beyond the code, and we do not promise either.

## What a well-built Wix app includes

- A dashboard page with clear settings, saved reliably, and helpful empty and error states.
- A site widget that can be added in the editor and shows correctly on desktop and phone.
- A settings panel so owners can adjust the widget without touching code.
- Data stored in a collection with sensible permissions.
- Backend logic for anything that should not run in the browser.
- Pricing plans configured in the Dev Center when the app is paid.
- Text prepared for translation, so new languages are easy to add.
- A test site where the install, use and update flow has been tried.
- A submission checklist covering what the App Market asks for.

## How we build your app

We start by agreeing the idea and the screens in writing, so nothing is built on assumption. Then we create the project with the Wix CLI in your repository, build the dashboard page and the widget, and connect them to a data collection. We install the app on a test site and walk through it as a new owner would.

The Basic package delivers one dashboard page and one widget. Standard widens this to several pages and widgets, adds pricing plans and owner-editable settings. Premium adds custom backend APIs, automated tests on the main flows, a draft listing and a period of bug fixes after delivery.

## What to do and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Describe the one problem your app solves in a single sentence.
- Share examples of apps you like and dislike.
- Decide early whether the app will be free or paid.
- Test the finished app on a real site before submitting.

**Avoid:**
- Demanding a full feature list before the first submission. A smaller, working app is easier to improve.
- Copying another app's layout, which can cause listing problems.
- Storing sensitive data you do not need.
- Skipping the phone check for the widget.

## Who this is for

A founder with an app idea and no developer. An agency that keeps rebuilding the same feature for clients and wants to package it. A business owner who wants their tool available to others in the App Market.

## What we need from you

A short brief with the problem, the target site owners and any design references. Add us as a collaborator on your Dev Center account and repository, so the code and the app stay yours from the first day. We never ask for your password. If you do not yet have a developer account, we will tell you how to create one, and you keep full ownership of it.
